IBM.rationale: IBM shows solid fundamental health with Q1 2026 revenue growth of 6% YoY, strong software (+8%) and infrastructure (+12%) performance, and record IBM Z quarter (+48%). Free cash flow grew 13% to $2.2B, the highest Q1 in a decade. Operating margins expanded 140bps and diluted operating EPS grew 19%. However, the stock has declined ~25% over the past quarter, and the P/E has compressed from ~40-50x to 20.5x, suggesting significant de-rating. The QoQ trajectory shows revenue and EPS declining sharply (rev -6.2%, EPS -44.6%), though this reflects Q2 2025's seasonally strong quarter rather than a fundamental deterioration. YoY metrics remain healthy. The balance sheet carries elevated debt ($57.7B long-term debt per filing) following the $11.6B Confluent acquisition, with total liabilities of $123B against $33B equity. Valuation at 20.5x P/E is near the low end of its 12-month range (20.1-51.2), making it cheap vs. its own history. However, consulting growth is sluggish (+1% CC), federal contract cancellations ($100M) create headwinds, and the Iran war is causing deal delays. The Q1 earnings beat ($1.91 vs $1.81 est.) was met with a 7-9% stock decline, indicating the market was disappointed by guidance maintenance rather than raises. No clear near-term catalyst exists to re-rate the stock, though the FedRAMP authorization of 11 AI products and the Confluent integration could provide medium-term tailwinds.
key_factors: Q1 2026 revenue +6% YoY with software +8% and infrastructure +12%; record IBM Z quarter (+48%)
Free cash flow $2.2B, up 13% YoY, highest Q1 in a decade; operating margin expansion of 140bps
P/E compressed to 20.5x from 40-50x range over past year, near 12-month low of 20.1x
Stock down ~25% in past quarter despite earnings beat, reflecting guidance disappointment and AI disruption concerns
Consulting growth sluggish at +1% CC with 15 federal contract cancellations ($100M) and Iran war deal delays
Balance sheet leverage elevated post-Confluent acquisition ($11.6B); long-term debt $57.7B
Generative AI book of business >$12.5B and ARR $24.6B (+10% YoY) provide medium-term revenue visibility
FedRAMP authorization of 11 AI products could unlock federal/regulated market opportunities
